---
title: "Reveal.js notes"
subtitle: "How hidden slides work in a deck."
description: "Learn how Veil removes hidden slides from the deck, and the limits with the chalkboard, auto-animate, and numeric hashes."
---

## Hidden slides leave the deck

Veil moves each hidden section out of `.slides`.
After each change it calls `Reveal.sync()`, so Reveal.js counts the slides again.
The slide numbers, the progress bar, the overview, and the slide menu follow.

- A hidden `#` stack leaves as a unit.
  If all the slides of a stack are hidden, the stack is hidden too.
- A shown slide comes back at its original place.
- If the current slide becomes hidden, the deck goes to the next visible slide, else to the previous visible slide.
- A fragment in hidden content does not count.

## Speaker view, multiplex, and scroll view

- All the windows of the speaker view must have the same state, because they synchronise by slide indices.
  A change in the main window goes to the speaker view.
- With multiplex, the master sends the state to each follower.
- Scroll view stops and starts again around a change.

## Limits

### Chalkboard

The chalkboard keeps drawings by slide indices.
After a change, a drawing can show on a different slide.
Choose the state before you draw.
Veil writes a warning when the chalkboard is enabled and the document has veiled slides.

### Auto-animate

Auto-animate can run between slides that become neighbours.
If this is not what you want, do not use auto-animate across slides that are in different groups.

### Numeric hashes

With `hash-type: number`, a hash such as `#/3` points to a slide index.
The index changes with the state.
Share the URL with the `veil` parameter to give the same deck to each reader.

### Two tabs

Two browser tabs of the same deck do not sync each other.
Each speaker view follows the deck that opened it.
